writeup.headline: Shopify rates Buy on fast growth, net cash and strong price trend, despite high absolute multiples.
writeup.thesis: Shopify scores 66, just 2 points above the Hold line, so it sits at the low edge of Buy. Growth is the main support, with TTM revenue growth of 32.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 33.7% year on year, though growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 on net cash with no debt, and quality is solid with a 17.7% FCF margin, 13.9% operating margin and diluted share count down 0.8% year on year. The share price trend is strong, with the price 29.5% above its 200-day average and shares 29.6 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation is the drag at a score of 32: in absolute terms the stock is expensive at 16.5x sales, 92.8x FCF and 115.7x EV/EBIT, even though it is cheap against its own history.
key_risks: High absolute multiples (92.8x FCF, 115.7x EV/EBIT) leave little room for a growth miss
Q3 results due November 3 could disappoint after analysts raised price targets
Growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter; further slowing would weigh on the growth score
Competition from Amazon and Google in AI-driven shopping
Ongoing Sezzle antitrust case and Briskin privacy class action
what_would_change: A drop of just 2 points, for example from weaker Q3 growth, softer news or a pullback in the price trend, would move the rating to Hold
Reaching Strong Buy needs 14 more points, most plausibly from a better valuation score or faster growth
A guidance raise or analyst upgrades on Q3 could lift the news risk score from 59
